question: Can international researchers get counseling in English?
required_facts: Yes: the KIRD program offers free counseling (up to 5 sessions, Zoom) with psychologists fluent in English
Eligibility: science and technology professionals with E/F-series visas or graduate students
OIA counseling is also offered in English (Korean, Chinese, English)
reference_answer: Yes. The KIRD Psychological Counseling for International Researchers program gives up to 5 free Zoom sessions with certified psychologists who are fluent in English; it is open to science and technology professionals with E- or F-series visas and to graduate students, so a doctoral student qualifies. The OIA counseling program also runs in English.
notes: Graduate eligibility matches the gold profile; degree_level does not change the yes (OIA counseling is in English for all), so no branch.

question: How do I book the international student counseling program?
required_facts: Seoul: visit the OIA or send an e-mail, fill in the application form, then an interview/test before counseling
Seoul contact: 02-2220-2450, International Building room 218, Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00
ERICA: book through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA booking route, campus unstated (Seoul gold profile)

reference_answer: It depends on your campus. At Seoul, visit the OIA (International Building room 218) or e-mail them, fill in the application form, and have an intake interview or test; phone 02-2220-2450, Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00. At ERICA, book through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing.
notes: Campus unstated and the booking route differs (8.3); two short branches.

question: How can I take the psychological health test?
required_facts: Seoul: log into HY-in > Foreign student > psychological health test (PHQ-9, 1-2 minutes, Korean/English/Chinese)
Seoul: offered in a set period each semester (March in 2026-1), for undergraduate and graduate students
ERICA: book psychological testing through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA testing route, campus unstated (Seoul gold profile)

reference_answer: At Seoul, log into HY-in > Foreign student > the psychological health test menu; it is the PHQ-9, takes 1-2 minutes, is available in Korean, English and Chinese, and runs in a set period each semester (throughout March in 2026-1). At ERICA, book psychological testing through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing.
notes: Campus unstated; the routes differ. The test window is semester-specific (latest found: March 2026); the procedure is the stable part. 2025-09 notice kept as outdated.

question: How do I apply to the international student group?
required_facts: Seoul (Global Love Hanyang): download the application form and submit it through the Google Form/QR link in the recruitment notice
Seoul eligibility: current Seoul undergraduates with at least one year left before graduation
ERICA (GLOBAL LOVE HYU): students fluent in Korean apply following e-mail notices sent every December

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA student group, campus unstated (Seoul gold profile)

reference_answer: At Seoul, the OIA student group (Global Love Hanyang) recruits current Seoul undergraduates with at least one year left; download the application form and submit it via the Google Form linked in the recruitment notice (latest: https://forms.gle/GJsmqre8FWpzAazr7), then a document review and interview follow. At ERICA, GLOBAL LOVE HYU takes students fluent in Korean and announces applications by e-mail every December.
notes: Hard: 'international student group' assumed = OIA ambassador group. 2026 (15th) notice has a Korean title and only a form link; stable rules taken from the 2025 English notice. One-year activity period may exclude a one-semester exchange student (caveat, outside vocabulary).

question: When is re-registration for spring 2026?
required_facts: Seoul 2026-1 re-registration: 2026.01.05-01.16, additional period 2026.02.12 only for Hanyang IIE Korean-course completers in Korea
ERICA 2026 spring return to school: 1st round Jan 7-18, 2026; 2nd round Feb 12-13, 2026 (IIE completers in Korea)

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA return-to-school dates, campus unstated (Seoul gold profile)

At ERICA, the spring 2026 return-to-school period was 7-18 January 2026, with a second round on 12-13 February 2026 for IIE completers in Korea.

question: Where do international students apply to return to the Seoul campus?
required_facts: Apply online through the HY-in portal re-registration page (upload passport and bank balance certificate)
In-person or e-mail applications at the OIA are not accepted
reference_answer: Seoul re-registration (return) is applied for online in the HY-in portal, where you upload your passport copy and bank balance certificate; applications in person at the OIA or by e-mail are not accepted. Questions go to the OIA at 82-2-2220-2445~2448.
notes: The 2026-1 guide's procedure screenshots are images; 'HY-In portal' is explicit only in the 2021 guide (outdated). Seoul campus stated.

question: How do I extend my residence card?
required_facts: Apply from 4 months before the visa expires, no later than the expiry date
Documents: application form, passport, ARC, certificate of enrollment, tuition receipt, transcript, proof of residence, KRW 60,000 fee
Seoul: get the OIA signature first (submit by 14:00, pick up 16:00) and visit OIA at least 3 days before the immigration appointment
reference_answer: Apply for the extension from 4 months before your visa expires and no later than the expiry date, at the immigration office with the application form, passport, ARC, certificate of enrollment, tuition receipt, last semester's transcript, proof of residence and the KRW 60,000 fee. At Seoul, book the immigration appointment first and bring the documents needing the OIA signature at least 3 days before (submitted by 14:00, ready at 16:00). Stay in Korea until the extension is approved.
notes: Extension rule is national (ERICA visa page); Seoul OIA signature step is a campus addition. Caveat: leaving Korea during the extension cancels it (4c207340, 2022).

question: Is there a winter school for international students?
required_facts: Yes: Hanyang International Winter School (HIWS) at the Seoul campus
Two 2-week sessions; 130+ courses taught in English plus cultural activities
Info at www.hanyangwinter.com, +82-2-2220-2453
reference_answer: Yes. Hanyang International Winter School (HIWS) on the Seoul campus offers two 2-week sessions with 130+ courses taught in English, cultural activities and a buddy program. See www.hanyangwinter.com or call +82-2-2220-2453.
notes: No ERICA winter school page; ERICA only mentions an Instagram account covering summer/winter school.

question: How can I reach the international office?
required_facts: Seoul OIA: International Building (#108), tel +82-2-2220-2453~2460, or the contact form
ERICA OIA: 3F Student Welfare Building, Mon-Fri 8:30-17:30 in semester

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA OIA contact, campus unstated (Seoul gold profile)

reference_answer: At Seoul, the OIA is in the International Building (#108), 222 Wangsimni-ro; call +82-2-2220-2453~2460 or use the contact form on the OIA site. At ERICA, the OIA is on the 3rd floor of the Student Welfare Building, open Mon-Fri 8:30-17:30 during the semester (lunch 12-13).
notes: Campus unstated; two short branches.

question: What happens during international student counseling month?
required_facts: A monthly program in January for graduate students (master's and Ph.D.) in English
About 10 students per session, on four topics; online application form
reference_answer: The counseling month notice describes a January program in English for graduate (master's and Ph.D.) students: sessions of about 10 international students on four topics, with an online application form. It comes from a December 2021 notice, so check the OIA board for the current program.
notes: Only a 2021 notice; descriptive, no term asked. Target group is graduate students while the persona is non-degree (caveat).

question: What should I know about illegal flyers around campus?
required_facts: Outside companies distribute illegal flyers (e.g. Korean education) in international buildings and on campus
Official school programs carry the department/team stamp; check it before joining
reference_answer: Outside companies often hand out illegal flyers, for example for Korean classes, in the international buildings and on campus. Official university programs carry the stamp of the international office or team, so check for it and avoid unofficial offers.

question: What documents do I need for alien registration at ERICA?
required_facts: Integrated application form, passport and copy, one 3.5x4.5 cm photo, certificate of enrollment, proof of residence
Processing fee KRW 30,000
Register within 90 days of entry; group application or book individually via HiKorea
reference_answer: Bring the integrated application form, your passport and a copy, one photo (3.5x4.5 cm, white background), a certificate of enrollment, proof of residence (lease, residence or dormitory confirmation) and the KRW 30,000 fee. Register within 90 days of entry, through the semester's group application or by booking an individual appointment on HiKorea.

question: When is the ERICA library open?
required_facts: General reading rooms (lobby, reading rooms, lounges) are open 24 hours
Resource reading rooms / loans: weekdays 09:00-21:00, Saturday 09:00-12:00 in semester; weekdays 10:00-17:00 in holidays
Closed on New Year's Day, Seollal and Chuseok (resource rooms also on Sundays and national holidays)
reference_answer: The ERICA Academic Information Center's general reading rooms are open 24 hours. The loans/returns and reference rooms open 09:00-21:00 on weekdays and 09:00-12:00 on Saturdays during the semester, and 10:00-17:00 on weekdays in vacations. General reading rooms close on New Year's Day, Seollal and Chuseok; resource rooms also close on Sundays and national holidays.

question: Does ERICA have an app or bot for campus information?
required_facts: Hanyangbot app: shuttle timetables, cafeteria meals, book info
HeyYoung Campus app: mobile student ID, attendance, academic administration
ERICA OIA KakaoTalk channel for visas, events, scholarships
reference_answer: Yes. Hanyangbot gives shuttle timetables, cafeteria menus and book information; the HeyYoung Campus app has the mobile student ID, attendance and academic administration; and the ERICA OIA KakaoTalk channel posts visa, event and scholarship news.

question: What documents are needed for a part-time work permit?
required_facts: Application form, passport, ARC, transcript or certificate of attendance, proof of Korean (or English) proficiency
Part-time work confirmation signed by the university's person in charge of international students
Business registration certificate copy and a standard employment contract (hourly wage, duties, hours)

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul OIA submission checklist; gold student is at ERICA

reference_answer: You need the application form, passport, ARC, a transcript or certificate of attendance, proof of Korean proficiency (or English scores for English-track students), the part-time work confirmation signed by the university's international-student officer, a copy of the employer's business registration certificate and a standard employment contract with wage, duties and hours. Manufacturing or construction employers need an extra compliance confirmation and the employer's ID copy.
notes: Document list is national; Seoul checklist is the same set with campus submission steps.

question: Can I get a psychological test at ERICA?
required_facts: Yes: ERICA's international student counseling center offers psychological testing (e.g. MMPI-2, SCT, MBTI, TCI, FCPI, Holland), free
Book through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing
reference_answer: Yes. ERICA's counseling center for international students offers free psychological testing (MMPI-2, SCT, MBTI, TCI, FCPI, Holland, plus group screening tests). Book it in HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing.

question: What field trips can exchange students join at ERICA?
required_facts: Everland trip for ERICA exchange/visiting students (fall 2024: Nov 10, 120 places, KRW 10,000)
The Lotte World trip was for degree students only; exchange students were not eligible
Field programs run 1-2 times per semester; apply at the OIA Welcome Desk
reference_answer: ERICA runs field programs 1-2 times a semester; you apply at the Welcome Desk in front of the OIA and pay the fee. The latest posted trip for exchange and visiting students was Everland (10 November 2024, 120 places, KRW 10,000 cash); the Lotte World trip was for degree students only, so exchange students could not join it.
notes: Trip notices are from fall 2024; the field-program page is undated. Lotte World span is gold per 9.6 (shows ineligibility).

question: Where can I eat on ERICA campus?
required_facts: Residential College Cafeteria (Residence Hall 1) and Student Cafeteria (Student Welfare Building 2F), KRW 4,000
Food Court (Student Welfare Building 3F), KRW 6,500-9,000; Faculty Cafeteria and Business Incubator cafeteria
reference_answer: ERICA has the Residential College Cafeteria (Residence Hall 1, three meals, KRW 4,000), the Student Cafeteria (Student Welfare Building 2F, lunch, KRW 4,000), the Food Court (Student Welfare Building 3F, KRW 6,500-9,000), the Faculty Cafeteria (3F, KRW 5,500-6,000) and the Hanyang Business Incubator cafeteria (B1F, KRW 5,500).

NHI is run by the Ministry of Health and Welfare; all inquiries go to the NHIS customer center 1577-1000
reference_answer: The university pages do not explain what happens to your National Health Insurance after graduation. NHI is run by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, not the university, so ask the NHIS customer center (1577-1000).

Refer to the Seoul OIA international admissions / the Undergraduate Admission Guide

Refer to the admission guide / OIA international admissions

question: Can I extend my residence card while I'm on leave?
required_facts: Students on leave must leave Korea within 30 days, whatever their visa validity
Students staying in Korea without attending are reported to immigration and can be fined
A D-2 extension requires a certificate of enrollment and tuition receipt
reference_answer: Generally no. Students who take a leave of absence must leave Korea within 30 days regardless of their visa's validity, and students who stay without attending are reported to immigration and can be fined. The D-2 extension also needs a certificate of enrollment and a tuition receipt, which you do not have while on leave. Check with the OIA if your case is special.
notes: Hard: no page says 'no extension on leave' outright; answer combines the 30-day departure rule (ERICA leave guide, immigration-related) with the extension document list. Treated as national.

question: Can a student on leave still receive an international scholarship?
required_facts: HIEA excludes students who took a leave of absence
The TOPIK scholarship also excludes students on leave

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA TOPIK scholarship; gold student is Seoul

reference_answer: No. HIEA is only for students currently attending, and explicitly excludes students who took a leave of absence; the TOPIK scholarship also says students on leave cannot apply. You can apply again after you re-register.
notes: Same on both campuses, so campus is not a branch.

question: Which insurance do I need while I'm on leave outside Korea?
required_facts: NHI premiums are waived for periods abroad of 1 month or more
Whether Hanyang's private insurance is needed while on leave abroad is not stated (only enrolled and completed-coursework cases)
reference_answer: For National Health Insurance, premiums are waived for any period you are out of Korea for a month or more. The current Seoul private-insurance notice only covers enrolled students (paid by the university) and completed-coursework students (25,000 won), not students on leave abroad, so ask the Seoul OIA whether you need anything before you return.
notes: 2025-1 re-registration insurance notice (Korean title, English body) is semester-specific, kept as outdated.

question: Which program should I choose if I'm coming for just one semester?
required_facts: Exchange program: for students nominated by a partner university, fee-waived, one or two semesters
Visiting student program: fee-paying, open to all, one or two semesters
reference_answer: Both programs allow one semester. If your home university is a Hanyang partner and nominates you, choose the Student Exchange Program (tuition waived); otherwise apply to the fee-paying Visiting Student Program.
notes: Partner nomination is outside the vocabulary, so it is a caveat, not a branch.

question: Do visiting students have to join Korean health insurance?
required_facts: NHI is mandatory for international students since March 2021; NHIS mails a bill to those eligible
Premium from March 2026: 79,320 won per month
Specific eligibility rules for visiting/short-stay students are not stated; NHIS handles all inquiries
reference_answer: National Health Insurance has been mandatory for international students since March 2021: NHIS mails a bill to everyone eligible (79,320 won a month from March 2026). The pages do not say whether a short visiting stay is covered, so confirm with NHIS (1577-1000).
notes: Hard: answer vs partial. No page names visiting students or the minimum stay.

question: I just got admitted. How do I apply for my student visa?
required_facts: Get the Certificate of Admission from your campus first (ERICA's CoA steps are not in the English snapshot)
Apply for D-2 at the Korean embassy (or immigration via HiKorea if in Korea) with CoA, business registration certificate, application form, passport, photo, TB test if required
After entry, register as an alien within 90 days

The English ERICA pages do not explain how ERICA issues the CoA to new students, so ask the ERICA OIA.
notes: Hard: campus unstated. Seoul CoA steps are campus-specific; D-2 documents treated as national. ERICA group-visa guide is an attachment not in the text.

question: Can I get an ERICA scholarship with TOPIK 1 if I'm in the English track?
required_facts: HIEA language rule: valid TOPIK, or IELTS/TOEFL for English-track students, so the language condition is met
HIEA needs grades from the previous semester at HYU and GPA >= 3.0 (undergraduate); new students are not yet eligible
TOPIK scholarship pays only for raising TOPIK (e.g. no TOPIK/level 3 or lower to level 4+: KRW 1,000,000)
reference_answer: For HIEA, English-track students may use IELTS or TOEFL instead of TOPIK (and TOPIK 1 is still a valid score), but you need grades from a previous semester at Hanyang with a GPA of at least 3.0, so a newly admitted student can apply only after the first semester; an enrolled student who meets the GPA can apply via HY-in in March or September. The TOPIK scholarship only rewards a higher TOPIK level than you submitted before, e.g. KRW 1,000,000 for reaching level 4 in non-arts programs.
notes: Branch = academic_status (admitted_not_enrolled vs enrolled), unstated; persona is newly admitted.
